chapter_title: The Making of a Global World

zero_omission_notes.summary: Global integration has deep historical roots. Pre-modern Silk Routes connected Asia, Europe, and Africa in trade (silk, spices, silver) and cultural exchange (religions, food like spaghetti/potatoes). Biological conquest via smallpox decimated Native Americans. In the 19th century, global trade was shaped by three economic flows (goods, labor, capital). British repeal of Corn Laws created global food markets, while refrigerated ships revolutionized meat trade. Late 19th-century imperialism saw Europe carve up Africa (1885 Berlin Conference) and Rinderpest (cattle plague) destroy African pastoral economies. Indentured labor supplied plantation workers under harsh terms. WWI transformed global finance, making US a creditor nation. Mass production (Henry Ford's assembly line) fueled the 1920s boom, but agricultural overproduction and the 1929 Wall Street Crash caused the Great Depression. Post-WWII stability was rebuilt via the 1944 Bretton Woods institutions (IMF and World Bank). Developing nations formed G-77 for a New International Economic Order (NIEO) before production relocated to low-wage Asian economies in the 1970s.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Pre-modern global interlinks existed through Silk Routes carrying Chinese silk, ceramics, Indian textiles, and West Asian silver. Food items migrated: noodles from China became spaghetti; potatoes, maize, tomatoes, and chillies traveled from post-Columbus Americas. European conquest of the Americas succeeded through biological warfare—smallpox germs to which indigenous populations lacked immunity.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Dissenter
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: One who refuses to accept established beliefs or practices.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Economists categorize three international flows: trade, labor, and capital. British repeal of Corn Laws enabled cheap food imports, causing agricultural land abandonment and emigration to America/Australia. Refrigerated ships (1870s) lowered meat prices in Europe. 1885 Berlin Conference partitioned Africa among European empires. Rinderpest (1880s cattle plague) killed 90% of African cattle, pushing pastoralists into wage labor.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Indentured Labour
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Bonded worker under contract to work for a specific employer for a set period.

detailed_sections.full_notes: WWI turned Britain into a debtor to the US. Henry Ford's Detroit assembly line mass-produced Model T cars ($5/day wage offset conveyor belt speed). Agricultural overproduction and the Oct 1929 Wall Street Crash caused the Great Depression: 4,000+ US banks collapsed, global trade halved, and Indian agricultural exports dropped 50%, forcing rural gold sales.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Bretton Woods (1944)
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Established IMF and World Bank to maintain fixed exchange rates pegged to US Dollar.

textbook_exercises.question: Explain the effects of the abolition of Corn Laws.
textbook_exercises.answer:
1. Cheap foreign grain flooded Britain, making domestic farming uncompetitive.
2. Farm workers lost employment and migrated to cities or overseas.
3. Lower food prices increased industrial growth and global agricultural expansion.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: Which conference created the IMF and World Bank in July 1944?
objective_questions_1_mark.explanation: Bretton Woods Conference in New Hampshire established the post-war international monetary framework.

short_answer_questions.question: What was the Multilateral Settlement System?
short_answer_questions.answer: A system where a country's trade deficit with one nation is settled using its trade surplus with another. Britain used its trade surplus in India to balance deficits with Western nations.

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Explain how Rinderpest aided European conquest of Africa.
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: Rinderpest wiped out 90% of African cattle, destroying the pastoral economy. Deprived of livestock livelihoods, Africans were forced into the wage labor market, allowing European colonizers to subjugate the continent easily.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Discuss the causes and global impacts of the Great Depression of 1929.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer:
Causes:
1. Post-WWI agricultural overproduction led to falling crop prices, prompting farmers to increase production and crashing markets.
2. Wall Street stock market crash (Oct 1929) caused US banks to recall foreign loans.
Impacts:
1. Over 4,000 US banks collapsed and global trade halved.
2. Unemployment rose to 25% in the US.
3. In India, agricultural prices dropped 50%, pushing peasants into debt and forced gold sales.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: Indian indentured laborers recruited for Caribbean plantations created hybrid cultural forms like Hosay carnival and Chutney music.

qa.question: Why did indentured workers develop hybrid cultural expressions?
qa.answer: Isolated in harsh plantation environments, workers combined native Indian traditions with local cultures to express solidarity and survival.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Believing 19th-century indentured labor was voluntary migration.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: Recruitment agents lied about working conditions and destinations, leading historians to term it a 'new system of slavery'.
